newsitem.title: USA: Amana may be a hard sell for Raytheon - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Amana may be a hard sell for Raytheon - analysts.

text.p: Raytheon Co is getting a cold reception from the appliance industry to its bid to sell its appliance division that includes the Amana brand, analysts said Monday.

"It's not going to be an easy sell," Cowen & Co analyst Jeffrey Sprague said. "Maytag (Co ) would be a perfect fit, but Maytag has spent a lot of its own money developing its own high-end refrigeration units."
S&P Equity Group's Robert Schpoont said, "It's not an easy sell. And Maytag's CEO (chief executive officer Leonard Hadley) said recently the company was into too many different businesses."

Maytag spokesman Thomas Schwartz, while declining to discuss any acquisitions, did note that the company just completed spending $180 million to rebuild a factory and launched a new line of refrigerators in February.
A Maytag spokesman could not be reached for comment.

Another likely suitor, General Electric Co "is too big. They would run into restraint of trade issues," Sprague said. General Electric declined to comment on any such deal. "We just don't speculate about acquisition targets," GE spokesman Vance Myer said. The company's last annual report showed operating profit from its appliance division was $750 million in 1996, up from $697 million in 1995.

"If it was an easy sale, we would have seen it sold already," H.G. Wellington analyst Wayne Johnson said. "The Street's been after them (Raytheon) for a while to sell it (the appliance division)...It's going to be a tough go."

Johnson speculated that Philips Electronics NV, the Netherlands-based electronics and appliance giant, might be interested in Amana. "They've wanted to break into the U.S. (appliance) market," he said.
Sprague speculated Samsung Electronics Co Ltd, the South Korean consumer electronics maker which also produces washing machines and microwave ovens, could be a taker.
"But then you have the problem of how much is somebody willing to pay for the number five slot in the (U.S.) industry?" Sprague said.
Raytheon reported its appliance division had first quarter sales of $341 million and operating profits of $13 million.
The Lexington, Massachusetts-based company has refocused its efforts to become a major player in the defense industry.
In the meantime, Raytheon has hired CS First Boston to help it evaluate selling or merging the appliance division.
